newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to start work in 1998 on Strasbourg link.
newsitem.headline: France to start work in 1998 on Strasbourg link.

text.p: Work will begin in 1998 on the first phase of a new high-speed rail line linking Paris with Strasbourg in northeastern France, the Transport Ministry announced on Monday.
No date was announced for completion of the costly project or its initial phase.
The first phase, when completed, will cut rail travel time between the two cities to two and a half hours from the current three hours and 51 minutes, the ministry said.
When the entire "TGV East" project is completed, the trip will be possible in just two hours.
In the first phase of the project, new track suitable for France's TGV high-speed trains will be built between Vaires in the Paris region and Vandieres, near the eastern cities of Metz and Nancy.

The government announced in October that it had decided to build the new $4 billion, 416-km (250-mile) line gradually over an unspecified period of time in order to stretch out costs. No starting date was disclosed at that time.
